claims.claim: The UK CMA on Friday opened a Competition Act 1998 investigation into whether Meta is abusing a dominant position through terms that could let it use publishers' and advertisers' content, including for AI.
claims.episode_span: opened a Competition Act 1998 investigation into whether Meta holds a dominant position
claims.source_title: CMA opens Meta investigation over use of publishers’ content for AI
claims.supporting_quote: The CMA announced the case on Friday under the Competition Act 1998.

claims.claim: Sarah Cardell said a company with a dominant position must not use that position to impose unfair terms.
claims.episode_span: a company with a dominant position must not use it to impose unfair terms
claims.source_title: CMA opens Meta investigation over use of publishers’ content for AI
claims.supporting_quote: But where a company holds a dominant position, it must not use that position to impose unfair terms,” said Sarah Cardell, the CMA’s chief executive.

claims.claim: Meta planned the new terms for 30 October, delayed them to 20 November, and on 28 October paused the rollout pending consultation.
claims.episode_span: planned the terms for 30 October, pushed them to 20 November
claims.source_title: CMA opens Meta investigation over use of publishers’ content for AI
claims.supporting_quote: Meta first planned to bring in the new terms on 30 October. It then pushed them back to 20 November, after talks with the CMA. On 28 October, it paused the rollout until it has consulted industry groups, the CMA said.

claims.claim: A Norwegian court temporarily banned Meta from enforcing the new terms after 10 media outlets challenged them.
claims.episode_span: a court earlier in the week temporarily banned Meta from enforcing the new terms after 10 media outlets
claims.source_title: CMA opens Meta investigation over use of publishers’ content for AI
claims.supporting_quote: In Norway, a court earlier in the week temporarily banned Meta from enforcing the new terms after 10 media outlets argued they threatened their rights to their content, Agence France-Presse reported.

claims.claim: Meta said there were no grounds for an investigation and that it had committed not to change terms without consulting publishers.
claims.episode_span: Meta said there were "no grounds" for an investigation
claims.source_title: CMA opens Meta investigation over use of publishers’ content for AI
claims.supporting_quote: Meta said there were “no grounds” for an investigation, Sam Tabahriti reported for Reuters.
